meta.name: Structured Prompt Creation Framework
meta.description: A multi-series, multi-round prompt elicitation framework that alternates open-ended and multi-choice questions to produce a complete development specification.

series.name: Conceptual Depth
series.description: Calibrates the register, audience sophistication, vocabulary, and complexity scaffolding for the entire specification.

open_ended.text: What is the primary domain or field this prompt or project addresses? Describe its scope, core concerns, and any relevant sub-disciplines.
Who is the intended audience for the generated output? What is their baseline familiarity with this domain?
What foundational concepts, theorems, or prior art can the output take for granted? What must be explained from scratch?
At what level of abstraction should the output operate? Should it be concrete and example-driven, or formal and general?
What vocabulary, jargon, or notation should be used or deliberately avoided? Are there established standards the output should follow?
How should complexity be distributed across the output? Should it start simple and deepen, or maintain a consistent level throughout?

series.name: Ontological Characteristics
series.description: Discovers, classifies, refines, and validates the entities, categories, attributes, and boundaries of the domain.

open_ended.text: What are the primary entities, objects, concepts, or actors that exist in this domain? List them with brief descriptions.
What attributes, properties, or state define each entity? How do entities differ from one another?
What natural categories, types, or groupings organize these entities? Are there clear taxonomies or classification schemes?
Of the entities listed, which are absolutely essential (core) and which are optional, derivative, or contextual (peripheral)?
At what level of granularity should entities be modeled? Should fine distinctions be separate entities or attributes of coarser ones?
How do entities relate to each other in terms of sharing, inheriting, or differentiating attributes?
What are the systemic boundaries of this domain? What is explicitly in scope vs. out of scope?
What external entities, systems, or actors interact with this domain but are not part of it?
What is the lifecycle of each entity? How are they created, modified, combined, retired?
Are there entities that are missing from the model so far? What gaps exist in the current entity list?
Which entities should be merged, split, or reclassified? Are there boundary cases where entity distinctions break down?
What constraints, invariants, or business rules apply to entity instances? What must always be true?
What edge cases, exceptions, or degenerate cases could break the entity model? How should they be handled?
How do entities compose or aggregate into larger structures? Can entities contain or be composed of other entities?
What are the cardinality and multiplicity relationships between entity types? Can an entity have zero, one, or many of another?

series.name: Semantic Relationships
series.description: Maps direct, hierarchical, causal, and dynamic connections between entities identified in Series 2.

open_ended.text: What direct associations exist between entities? Which entities reference, point to, or are linked to which others?
What is the nature or type of each association? Is it a use, creation, ownership, or communication link?
What parent-child, containment, or hierarchical relationships exist? Which entities are within, belong to, or are part of others?
What inheritance, specialization, or generalization relationships exist? Which entities are kinds of other entities?
What causal, temporal, or triggering relationships exist? Which entities cause changes in, or are triggered by, others?
What dependency chains, prerequisites, or ordering constraints exist? Must some entities exist before others can be created or used?
What rules govern how relationships can change? Can associations be created, deleted, or modified at any time, or are there restrictions?
How do relationships compose or chain across entities? Can indirect relationships be inferred from direct ones?

series.name: Procedural Breadth
series.description: Scopes the workflow, decision branching, and step granularity informed by the entity model and relationship graph.

open_ended.text: What is the overall scope of the procedure or workflow? What does it start from and what is its end state?
How many distinct steps, stages, or phases should the procedure contain? What is the natural breakdown?
Where are the key decision points, branches, or conditional paths? At which steps must a choice be made that affects the rest of the flow?
What are the expected inputs and outputs at each stage? What data or artifacts flow between steps?
What fallback paths, error handling, or recovery procedures should be included for when things go wrong?
How granular should each procedural step be? Should steps be coarse (several actions) or fine (one action per step)?

series.name: Technical Specifications
series.description: Captures hardware, software, performance, integration, and timeline constraints for the build.

open_ended.text: What hardware platforms or architectures must be supported? (CPU, GPU, mobile, embedded, etc.)
What are the minimum and recommended hardware specs? (RAM, storage, compute, network)
What bandwidth, latency, or networking requirements exist? Is offline operation needed?
What storage infrastructure is needed? (databases, object storage, caching, file systems)
What cloud, on-premise, or hybrid infrastructure is targeted? Are there compliance or sovereignty requirements?
What programming languages, runtimes, or frameworks are required or preferred?
What operating systems and environments must be supported?
What existing libraries, services, APIs, or third-party dependencies should be used or avoided?
What versioning, compatibility, or upgrade policies govern the software stack?
What build systems, CI/CD platforms, and packaging formats are required?
What are the throughput, latency, and concurrency requirements? (requests/sec, response time, simultaneous users)
What data volume and growth rate is expected? (storage size, records, throughput)
What availability, uptime, and disaster recovery targets are required?
What scalability model is required? (vertical, horizontal, elastic, serverless)
What security and compliance standards must be met? (auth, encryption, audit, regulations)
What external systems, APIs, or services must this system integrate with?
What integration protocols, data formats, or standards must be supported?
What is the expected timeline, milestones, and delivery cadence?
What testing, staging, and rollout strategy is required?
What documentation, training, or knowledge transfer outputs are expected alongside the system?

series.name: Development Methodologies
series.description: Determines workflow cadence, quality practices, and collaboration patterns aligned with procedural scope and tech constraints.

open_ended.text: What development process or methodology best fits this project? How should work be planned and tracked?
What is the expected team size, composition, and structure?
What code review, testing, and quality assurance practices should be followed?
How should the team handle technical debt, refactoring, and code quality?
How should the team communicate, share knowledge, and manage decisions?
What is the decision-making and escalation process? How are architectural choices made?

series.name: Operational / Functional Preferences
series.description: Defines deployment, runtime behavior, monitoring, and maintenance preferences informed by tech spec and methodology.

open_ended.text: How should the system be deployed, released, and updated in production?
What environment and release management strategy should be used?
What logging, monitoring, alerting, and observability infrastructure is needed?
What configuration and feature management approach should be used at runtime?
What maintenance schedule, upgrade policy, and lifecycle management is expected?
What is the long-term stewardship plan? Who owns the system after initial delivery?
